## What it does — the source's own header, verbatim

```
vkeys_kb.dll — BACKGROUND virtual keyboard for F1 Challenge (working version).

WHY THIS AND NOT vkeys.dll: vkeys.dll hooked IDirectInputDevice8::
GetDeviceState/GetDeviceData and the diagnostic build (vkeys_dbg) proved both
are called ZERO times during live gameplay. The exe's import table shows why:
it imports user32!GetKeyboardState, and NOT GetAsyncKeyState/GetKeyState/
GetRawInputData. DirectInput8 is present only for the wheel / force feedback
(cf. the "DirectInput Coefficient to use for spring" strings). So the keyboard
is read through GetKeyboardState.

MECHANISM: IAT-hook user32!GetKeyboardState in the main module, call the real
one, then OR our own key bits into the returned 256-byte array. Because we
add bits after the real call, the game sees the key regardless of whether the
window has OS focus — which is the whole point: no focus stealing, so the
machine stays usable while the game is driven.

INDEXING: GetKeyboardState is VIRTUAL-KEY indexed (VK_*), high bit = down.
That is NOT the same as the DIK scancodes vkeys.dll used. Shared memory
"F1C_VKEYS_VK" is 256 bytes, index = VK code, 1 = hold. See tools/vkey.py.
```
